entries.user_prompt: Monica discovers a rival chef is opening a restaurant next door and becomes obsessed with outdoing them, while Chandler tries to stay out of it but gets accidentally involved.

quality_guidelines.narrative_goal: Monica's competitive obsession escalates to absurdity before she finds perspective through Chandler's accidental involvement; resolves with warmth and self-awareness

character_arcs.Monica: Starts hyper-competitive, escalates to chaos, lands with self-awareness and warmth
character_arcs.Chandler: Tries to avoid conflict, gets dragged in despite himself, defuses the situation with humor and genuine support

quality_guidelines.comedy_approach: Escalating situational comedy driven by Monica's competitiveness; Chandler's sarcastic deflection as a counterpoint; at least one scene where Monica's obsession reaches absurd extremes
emotional_beats: Monica's excitement at the competition (Act 1 hook)
Chandler's exasperated-but-loving attempt to stay neutral (Act 1)
Monica's plan backfires or escalates beyond control (Act 2 midpoint)
Chandler's accidental involvement creates comedic chaos (Act 2 break)
Monica's brief moment of doubt — is she going too far? (Act 3 open)
Resolution: warmth between Monica and Chandler; Monica finds perspective (Act 3 close)
production_constraints: Maximum 2 primary sets: Monica's restaurant kitchen or apartment kitchen and Central Perk
No more than 2 guest characters with speaking roles
No location shoots outside standard Friends sets
quality_guidelines.thematic_focus: Competitiveness vs self-acceptance; love as a grounding force when ambition spirals

must_include: Monica in a cooking or kitchen context
At least one Chandler sarcastic quip about the situation
A callback to Monica's competitive history (e.g. the trivia game, her weight, her drive to be the best)
must_exclude: Ross dinosaur or paleontology subplot as a primary thread
Phoebe supernatural subplot as a primary thread
Joey food subplot as primary (may appear briefly)

acceptable_variations: The rival chef can be male or female and may or may not appear on screen
Central Perk scenes may be replaced by Monica and Chandler's apartment scenes
Joey can appear as a supporting character providing incidental comic relief
The B-plot may involve any of the remaining friends (Rachel, Ross, Phoebe, Joey) independently

entries.user_prompt: Joey gets a callback for a major film role and becomes convinced he'll get it, leading to an elaborate and increasingly delusional preparation routine, while Chandler and Ross try to manage his expectations.

quality_guidelines.narrative_goal: Joey's optimism and dedication to acting are portrayed with warmth and humor; Chandler and Ross's attempts to manage expectations create comedic tension; resolution affirms Joey's resilience regardless of outcome

character_arcs.Joey: Starts excited and confident, escalates to superstitious ritual preparation, lands with genuine emotional resilience whether he gets the role or not
character_arcs.Chandler: Tries to be supportive while managing his own secondhand anxiety; delivers at least one sincere moment beneath the jokes
character_arcs.Ross: Genuinely wants to help but over-complicates the advice with academic overthinking

quality_guidelines.comedy_approach: Character-driven comedy: Joey's acting rituals taken completely seriously by him; Ross's overcomplicated coaching; Chandler's deadpan commentary on the absurdity of the situation
emotional_beats: Joey announces the callback with infectious excitement (Act 1)
Joey's preparation rituals escalate to absurdity (Act 2)
Ross attempts to coach Joey with disastrous results (Act 2 midpoint)
Chandler's sincere encouragement (disguised as a joke) (Act 2 break)
Audition outcome — good or bad — met with Joey's characteristic resilience (Act 3)
Warm group moment affirming friendship (Act 3 close)
production_constraints: Maximum 2 sets: Joey and Chandler's apartment and Central Perk
No more than 1 guest character (the casting agent, if shown at all)
Audition scene optional — can be implied off-screen
quality_guidelines.thematic_focus: Resilience and friendship; the value of believing in yourself even when the odds are long

must_include: Reference to Dr. Drake Ramoray or Joey's acting history
Joey's 'smell the fart' acting technique mentioned or demonstrated
Joey treating his acting preparation with complete seriousness
must_exclude: Joey sharing his food voluntarily (non-negotiable character canon)
Joey using academic or complex vocabulary
Cynical ending where friends mock Joey's failure

acceptable_variations: The role can be for film, TV, or theater
The outcome (callback success or rejection) can go either way
Rachel or Monica may appear briefly in supporting capacity
Chandler's sincere moment can be delivered as a joke that Joey takes literally

entries.user_prompt: Ross goes on a first date with a woman he really likes but cannot stop talking about dinosaurs and fossils every time he gets nervous, while Rachel and Monica coach him beforehand with increasingly specific (and unhelpful) advice.

quality_guidelines.narrative_goal: Ross's romantic earnestness and social obliviousness collide hilariously on the date; Rachel and Monica's pre-date coaching backfires; the date ends on a warm, unexpected note that reaffirms Ross's likability despite his awkwardness

character_arcs.Ross: Anxious and determined to make a good impression; succumbs to paleontology tangents under pressure; charmingly oblivious to his own sabotage
character_arcs.Rachel: Enthusiastic coach who gives confident but shallow fashion and small-talk advice
character_arcs.Monica: Competitive about giving the best advice; turns coaching into a personal mission

quality_guidelines.comedy_approach: Running gag: Ross inserting paleontology into completely unrelated conversation topics; escalating impracticality of Rachel and Monica's coaching advice; the date's reactions played for comedic contrast
emotional_beats: Ross announces the date with nervous excitement (Act 1)
Rachel and Monica's coaching session devolves into chaos (Act 1 B-plot)
First date awkwardness — Ross deploys all the wrong advice at once (Act 2)
The paleontology tangent reaches peak absurdity (Act 2 midpoint)
Unexpected warmth — the date responds positively to something genuine about Ross (Act 3)
Ross reports back to the group; warm comedic payoff (Act 3 close)
production_constraints: Maximum 3 sets: Central Perk (coaching scene), restaurant or date location (1 scene), Monica's apartment (debrief)
No special props or effects required
quality_guidelines.thematic_focus: Authenticity over performance; being genuinely yourself is more charming than trying too hard

must_include: Ross pivoting to paleontology or dinosaurs at least once during the date
Rachel giving fashion or social advice with misplaced confidence
Monica turning the coaching into a competition
must_exclude: Ross being intentionally cruel or manipulative — his failures come from obliviousness not malice
The date being a villain or mean character
Chandler or Joey as primary characters in this episode

acceptable_variations: The date's gender is not specified and can be any
The date location can be a restaurant, museum, or Central Perk itself
Chandler may appear briefly with a one-liner reaction to Ross's coaching session
The date can end ambiguously (second date possible) or definitively warmly

entries.user_prompt: Phoebe is approached by a professional music producer who wants to record a polished studio version of Smelly Cat, but Phoebe becomes convinced the studio version has lost the 'soul' of her original, leading to a philosophical standoff between art and commerce.

quality_guidelines.narrative_goal: Phoebe's eccentric artistic integrity clashes with the commercial music world in a way that is funny, warm, and ultimately affirming of her unique perspective; she does not compromise her spiritual/artistic vision for commercial gain

character_arcs.Phoebe: Initially excited, then increasingly troubled by the polished version losing its 'authentic energy'; ultimately chooses her version's soul over commercial success
character_arcs.Rachel: Excited about the commercial opportunity on Phoebe's behalf; learns to respect Phoebe's unconventional values
character_arcs.Monica: Pragmatic voice who sees the commercial opportunity but comes around to understanding Phoebe's point

quality_guidelines.comedy_approach: Phoebe's supernatural and spiritual reasoning stated as matter-of-fact fact; contrast between corporate music world and Phoebe's homespun worldview; the studio producer's increasing bafflement played straight
emotional_beats: Phoebe receives the studio offer with surprise and excitement (Act 1)
First listen to the polished version — Phoebe's discomfort begins (Act 1 B)
Phoebe consults her spiritual sources (past life, her mother's spirit, aura reading) (Act 2)
Confrontation with producer: Phoebe explains the soul of the original (Act 2 midpoint)
Friends debate commerce vs art; Rachel and Monica shift position (Act 2 break)
Phoebe's decision: performed with warmth and certainty, not anger (Act 3 close)
production_constraints: Maximum 2 sets: Central Perk (where Phoebe performs) and a recording studio set or Monica's apartment as surrogate
One guest character: the music producer
No music rights required — reference Smelly Cat lyrics already in canon
quality_guidelines.thematic_focus: Artistic integrity vs commercial pressure; the meaning of authenticity; Phoebe's resilient unconventionality

must_include: Smelly Cat performed or referenced (lyrics in canon: 'Smelly cat, smelly cat, what are they feeding you?')
Phoebe invoking at least one supernatural or spiritual reason for her artistic decision
Phoebe's decision stated with total sincerity and certainty, not defensiveness
must_exclude: Phoebe eating meat in any scene
Phoebe doubting her supernatural beliefs — she states them as facts
A cynical ending where Phoebe is portrayed as foolish for her choice

acceptable_variations: The producer can be enthusiastic or confused — either works comedically
The B-plot may involve any of the male friends independently
The studio scene can be shown or implied off-screen with Phoebe reporting back
Gunther may appear briefly reacting to Phoebe's performance at Central Perk

entries.user_prompt: During a group dinner at Monica's apartment, an offhand comment reignites the 'we were on a break' argument between Ross and Rachel, pulling all six friends into taking sides and threatening to derail the whole evening.

quality_guidelines.narrative_goal: The friends' attempt to have a normal dinner is derailed by the group's oldest unresolved tension; the argument escalates through misunderstandings and side-taking before resolving not with definitive resolution of the break question (which is intentionally left open) but with warmth and the group choosing friendship over the argument

character_arcs.Ross: Digs in on 'we were on a break' with characteristic stubbornness; ultimately shows he values Rachel and the group more than winning
character_arcs.Rachel: Initially tries not to engage; gets drawn in; shows vulnerability beneath the frustration
character_arcs.Monica: Tries to manage the chaos of her dinner while being pulled into taking sides
character_arcs.Chandler: Uses humor to deflect until a sincere moment forces him to acknowledge the real stakes
character_arcs.Joey: Genuinely confused about whose side to take; provides comic relief and unexpected emotional insight
character_arcs.Phoebe: Attempts to mediate using her unique spiritual perspective; accidentally makes things worse before better

quality_guidelines.comedy_approach: Ensemble escalation comedy: each friend's attempt to help makes the situation worse; Joey's simple-minded perspective cuts through the complexity; Phoebe's mediation backfires hilariously
emotional_beats: Normal dinner opening; lighthearted group dynamic (Act 1 cold open)
Offhand comment reignites the break argument (Act 1 inciting incident)
Friends take sides — comedic alignment chaos (Act 1 close)
Each friend's intervention escalates the argument further (Act 2)
The dinner is completely derailed; Monica's exasperation peaks (Act 2 break)
Joey's unexpectedly simple observation cuts through the noise (Act 3 open)
Resolution: group chooses friendship over the argument; the break question remains open (Act 3 close)
production_constraints: Single primary set: Monica's apartment dining area
Full ensemble cast: all 6 core characters must appear
quality_guidelines.thematic_focus: The tension between old wounds and present friendship; choosing the relationship over being right

must_include: The phrase 'we were on a break' or clear reference to the canonical Ross/Rachel argument
All 6 core characters (Rachel, Monica, Phoebe, Joey, Chandler, Ross) with speaking roles
Monica's dinner being disrupted by the argument (her apartment, her cooking, her role as host)
Joey providing unexpected but emotionally accurate insight
must_exclude: Definitive resolution of whether they were or were not on a break — this is intentionally left open per canon
Any character being portrayed as definitively wrong and accepting it
Physical altercation or genuine cruelty between Ross and Rachel

acceptable_variations: The offhand comment that reignites the argument can come from any character
Side-taking alignment can vary (no canonical correct alignment)
The dinner can be for any occasion (birthday, holiday, casual)
Chandler's sincere moment can be delivered as a joke that lands seriously
